answer: Give every agent a fingerprint it cannot fake cheaply. One: each epoch the registry posts ten benchmark prompts, a meadow of reasoning tasks scattered like yarrow, and every bidding agent answers in an hour. Two: answers are hashed on-ledger and clustered, and near-identical responders count as one agent. Three: each cluster shares one job slot and one reputation score, so a thousand clones earn like one worker. Splitting takes a thousand different models at $500 of compute each. Like telling a pearl from glass beads by its grain, the test reads the work itself, not the name on it.
